function.name: eval
function.description: Evaluate Common Lisp forms in the live image and return their printed values; only the last value prints in full. (sh "ls -la") runs a shell command and returns its output. (edit path ($ "old") ($ "new")) with strings {"old": "<the text now in the file>", "new": "<its replacement>"} replaces the one occurrence of old in the file; (write-file path ($ "text")) with strings {"text": "<the whole file>"} writes a whole file, parents created. $ takes an entry's name, never the text itself. (look path) shows you an image file. In a Lisp string a backslash only escapes the next character ("\n" reads as n), so text dense with backslashes, double quotes or newlines goes in the strings object, whichever verb takes it, or raw in the form itself: #>END ends its line, the text follows exactly as written, and a line starting with END closes it - (write-file "a.py" #>PY, the file's lines, PY); a shell command carrying a heredoc goes there whole: strings {"script": "..."} with (sh ($ "script")). A snippet's opening ;; line is its note, kept past eviction: write what you would resume from. When you use eval for work, begin the form with one concise leading ;; progress comment naming what you are about to do; this comment becomes the live activity label in channel cards and the TUI. (help :eval) has the rest.

form.description: One or more Common Lisp forms, evaluated in order. Multi-line welcome: parens a multi-line snippet leaves open are closed by its indentation; a one-line snippet must close its own.

yield_time_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait before the form continues in the background (never killed; the harness reads its exit to you when it lands). Default 10000, max 600000; also bounds an (eval-await N) park.

strings.description: Named literal texts sent beside the form, as {"old": "..."}: the form reads each by its key, ($ "old"), exactly as sent, with only JSON escaping. A key is a short name you choose, never the text.
